references.text: Psalm 22:18 describes a scene where they divide the clothes of the suffering one and cast lots for them, which parallels the soldiers' actions toward Jesus in Matthew 27:29, where they also mock him.
Isaiah 53:3 prophesies about one who is despised and rejected, a suffering that Jesus experiences in Matthew 27:29 when he is mocked as 'King of the Jews'.

Isaiah 50:6 speaks of giving one's back to those who strike and one's cheeks to those who pull out the beard, a prediction of the mistreatment Jesus would endure, which aligns with the mockery and abuse in Matthew 27:29.
Luke 23:11 describes how Herod and his soldiers mocked Jesus by dressing him in an elegant robe, paralleling the soldiers' actions in Matthew 27:29.
Mark 15:17 also describes how the soldiers wove a crown of thorns and placed it on Jesus' head, directly parallel to the events in Matthew 27:29.
John 19:2-3 also describes how the soldiers wove a crown of thorns, placed it on Jesus' head, and mocked him as 'King of the Jews', paralleling Matthew 27:29.
